results.content: i “I AM A POPULARIST”: A CRITICAL DISCOURSE ANALYSIS OF THE POPULIST RHETORIC OF DONALD TRUMP’S PRESIDENTIAL CAMPAIGN A DISSERTATION SUBMITTED TO THE GRADUATE DIVISION OF THE UNIVERSITY OF HAWAIʻI AT MĀNOA IN PARTIAL FULFILLMENT OF THE REQUIREMENT FOR THE DEGREE OF DOCTOR OF PHILOSOPHY IN ENGLISH August 2020 By Cornelius Rubsamen Dissertation Committee: Daphne Desser, Chairperson Darin Payne Todd Sammons John Zuern Ned Bertz Keywords: Critical Discourse Analysis, Campaign Rallies, Donald Trump, Habitus, Identification, Populism, Rhetoric, Social Media, Style, Twitter ii ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS Writing this dissertation would not have been possible without the supportive faculty at the University of Hawaiʻi and the backing of my family. iii ABSTRACT The recent global rise of right-wing populism, as illustrated by the Brexit referendum in Great Britain and the election of Donald Trump in the United States, has become the subject of intense debate among academics. It then performs a textual analysis of three Trump campaign speeches in order to first operationalize the definition of populism and subsequently to answer the question, is Trump a populist?
